Upright frontal film: thin white line paralleling the left chest wall with no lung markings beyond it and darker spaces between the left ribs; heart and trachea in normal position. CT: a small ruptured bleb at the left apex.

A 78-year-old man with a recent stroke and poor swallow coughed repeatedly while a feeding catheter was passed through his nose. Feeds were started; 6 hours later he has T 38.3 C, RR 28, SpO2 88% and new crackles at the left base.

Film: radiopaque tip loops into the right and then the left main bronchus instead of passing below the left hemidiaphragm into the gastric gas bubble; after feeds, a new white density behind the heart has erased the left hemidiaphragm outline.

A 54-year-old woman with metastatic breast cancer has 6 weeks of progressive exertional dyspnea and fatigue. HR 104, BP 118/76, RR 20; JVP 9 cm, soft distant heart sounds; lungs clear, no crackles; no leg edema.
Film: enlarged heart; white airspace opacity fanning out from both hila with the apices and the lung bases relatively spared; lung markings crowd the outer third of both lungs.

A 68-year-old man 2 days after upper abdominal surgery takes shallow breaths because of incision pain and has a weak cough with thick secretions. T 37.8 C, RR 24, SpO2 91%; WBC 8,900/mm3; reduced breath sounds and dullness at the right base.

Film: white right lower zone with loss of volume - the right hemidiaphragm sits higher than the left and the lung reaches less far down; no air-filled bronchi within it and no curved fluid edge up the chest wall. Bronchoscopy: a mucus plug.

Frontal film: fluffy density behind the heart erasing the left hemidiaphragm and paraspinal outline, left heart border still sharp; no volume loss; air-filled bronchi within it. Lateral: vertebral bodies get whiter instead of darker going down.
